_about: Sprite framework: the shared rules every creature drawing follows, so the studio and the game agree on size, center and mouth. A species framework copies 'default' and overrides only what it needs.

default.name: Standard creature
rules: Face right. The game flips the drawing when the creature swims left.
The center of the canvas is the center of the body: the creature turns around this point and its hitbox circle sits here.
Keep the margin empty on every side, in every frame, so outlines, tail swings and open jaws never get cut off.
Put the mouth marker where the creature eats. The game uses it for eating and biting.
Draw at least one frame in idle or move. Empty poses fall back to idle.

crocodile.name: Crocodile
crocodile.notes: Wide and tall so the long snout, an open jaw and a tail curling up all fit with room to spare, even at level 30. Every stage uses this same canvas: a small hatchling simply leaves more empty space.

fish.name: Fish
fish.notes: Small and medium reef fish (Blue Tang, Reef Snapper). About 3.5 world pixels per art pixel in the game.

bigfish.name: Big fish
bigfish.notes: Large reef fish such as the Red Grouper.

shark.name: Shark
shark.notes: Long predators: room for a tall dorsal fin and a crescent tail.

mosa.name: Mosa
mosa.notes: Mike's long sea reptile. Wide for the long snout and tail, tall so the tail can curl up or down while swimming. Every stage uses this canvas; the eye stays in the same place in every frame so the mouth does not jump.

white_shark.name: White Shark
white_shark.notes: The third playable hero, drawn in the same style as Mike's Croc and Mosa. Tall enough for the dorsal fin, the crescent tail swinging up and down, and the eggshell and cap on the hatchling. The eye stays in the same place in every frame so the mouth does not jump.

crab.name: Crab
crab.notes: The Checkpoint Crab, seen from the front (it scuttles sideways). Wide for both claws, tall for the eye stalks, claws and legs. The game keeps it upright: it never tilts, it only turns left and right.

whale.name: Whale
whale.notes: The biggest creatures (Sperm Whale): long body, square head, flukes that swing up and down. About 5 world pixels per art pixel.

fang.name: Elder Shark
fang.notes: The fourth playable hero, the Elder Shark (called Fang until Nov 26; the id stays 'fang' so saves keep working): a pixel-art great white from Rhopers' sheets, converted by tools/fang/convert_fang.py, with the swim from his Nov 26 sheet (tools/fang/update_swim.py). Long, with room above and below for the tail curving down while it swims. The snout stays in the same place in every frame so the mouth does not jump.

elder_croc.name: Elder Croc
elder_croc.notes: The fifth playable hero: a pixel-art crocodile from a sheet of poses (idle, walk, bite, hurt), converted by tools/elder/convert_elder.py. Long poses for swimming and biting, standing poses for the level-up roar and the hurt flash, so the canvas is tall enough for both. The snout stays in the same place in the swim and bite frames.

spino.name: Spino
spino.notes: The sixth playable hero: Mike's brown spinosaurus with a tall sail, one sheet per stage (the hatchling inside its egg, the adult with yellow stripes), each with idle, swim, swim attack and hurt facing left, converted by tools/spino/convert_spino.py with the Sprite Studio skin engine (skinmaker.js). Long and low with room for the sail; the snout stays put in the swim and bite frames.
